- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or corrections — adjust downward bias in 3–5 day horizon.
- Overshoots in early forecast windows (1–7 days) often overreact to sentiment — dampen initial slope.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- Sentiment decay > 0.30 in 3–5 days triggers downward correction — reduce forecast by 2–5% per day of declining sentiment.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day horizon — if sentiment is low or flat, cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 14-day high.
